summary.headline: Digitide Q1 FY27 revenue rose 5.3% YoY to INR775 crore but fell 3.1% QoQ, with EBITDA margin at 9.9% and TCV bookings of INR205 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue was INR775 crore, up 5.3% YoY and down 3.1% QoQ, as management deliberately walked away from low-margin work and book-to-bill slipped. Reported EBITDA was INR76.9 crore (9.9% margin), down about INR11 crore QoQ, of which INR9.9 crore was a one-off lease-related item in Q4 and about INR10 crore was new wage costs under labour codes and state minimum wage revisions. Reported PAT was INR2.9 crore with no exceptionals, the first positive group PAT after two quarters. Management called Q1 the margin trough and reiterated a 200 bps EBITDA margin expansion for FY27, while de-emphasising the revenue target.

financial_highlights.change: Down about INR11 crore QoQ; like-to-like operating decline about INR1 crore
Up INR1 crore QoQ from INR21 crore
Positive after two quarters; no exceptional items

financial_highlights.value: INR55 crore (about INR36 crore ROU, INR19 crore owned/intangible)
financial_highlights.change: Normalised guidance INR55-57 crore per quarter

financial_highlights.value: INR15 crore (about INR11 crore lease interest)

segments.name: Tech and Digital
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR237 crore, 31% of total, growing 20.3% YoY. Management reports AI-led revenue of about INR15 crore (roughly 2% of revenue) from new AI projects; AI work inside BPM/T&D is not reported separately.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR296 crore, 38% of total, growing 10.2% YoY.

segments.name: BPM (India and West)
segments.commentary: Management describes it as margin-dilutive and resource-intensive in parts; deliberately selective on pursuits and repricing legacy contracts. Sequential decline cited by analysts; no segment revenue figure given in the call.

segments.name: Alldigi (standalone exclusion)
segments.commentary: Analyst cited standalone margin of about 5% excluding Alldigi; management said Q4 included dividend income not repeated in Q1. Management says Digitide standalone optics understate group profitability due to centrally held costs.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin expansion of 200 bps reiterated; management says Q1 is the margin trough.
Lease cash outflows for FY27 guided at INR175-180 crore, unchanged.
Normalised D&A guided at INR55-57 crore per quarter.
Double-digit FY27 revenue growth guidance not reaffirmed; management asked investors to measure on profitability growth rather than revenue.
USD 1 billion revenue ambition by FY31 retained as 'North Star' but not to be pursued at expense of profitability; no revised percentage growth path given yet.
Headcount (about 55,000) expected to decline over the next few quarters.
M&A to be pursued as 2-3 targeted acquisitions rather than one large deal; management says equity dilution is not an option being considered.
capex_capacity: About 55,000 employees mapped to business units; headcount on a declining trend as Tech and Digital grows and productivity improves.

Four-part operating model: business units, service lines, two go-to-market forces (West: US and Canada; India Plus), and consolidated corporate functions with a new COO office alongside the CFO office.
Platforms: payroll, insurance and collections; AI and cloud professional services (six new clients signed in the quarter); about 5.7 million AI interactions at 80-85% containment.
AI funnel of INR100-150 crore being chased; management open to a separate AI business unit with its own P&L at a future date.
No immediate plan to monetise land and buildings, which management says are held for operating use.
Lease renewal in March quarter capitalised as right-of-use asset.
demand_pricing: TCV bookings INR205 crore vs management ambition, with book-to-bill of about 11-13% in the quarter.
Customers deferring some planned bookings and billing into Q2 and Q3.
Wage cost step-up of about INR10 crore per quarter from new labour codes and state minimum wage revisions effective 1 April; active client repricing and cost-of-living adjustment talks underway.
Three large international deals being shaped with hyperscalers.
Verticals prioritised: BFS (India and West), insurance (US mid-market), healthcare; small presence in oil and gas and CMT in the US.
Management says competition in insurance is intense; approach is curated qualification of RFPs, not catch-all.

qa_highlights.question: Standalone margin ex-Alldigi around 5%; what is the forward margin and how much of the ~INR500 crore quarterly book has converted?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 standalone included dividend income not repeated in Q1, so the comparison is not like-for-like. Book-to-bill was 11-13% and some bookings slipped to Q2/Q3; some legacy contracts are being renegotiated.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR9,000 crore FY30/31 revenue target, including INR1,800 crore inorganic, be funded, and will there be dilution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will pursue build-partner-acquire, with two or three acquisitions rather than one large deal. Equity dilution is not an option the management team is pursuing; no land monetisation is planned.

qa_highlights.question: Why has performance deteriorated since demerger and what verticals offer good margin growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management framed the period as Chapter 3 of the company, with strategy unchanged but execution, accountability and walking away from weak accounts emphasised. Tech and Digital tracks are payroll, insurance and collections platforms, AI and cloud services, and AI within BPM.

qa_highlights.question: Should Alldigi be merged, and will margins return to pre-demerger levels?
qa_highlights.answer: The board will decide on any legal merger at an appropriate time with no timeline. Management said Digitide's central costs and capabilities are interlocked with Alldigi and that the group should be viewed on a consolidated basis.

qa_highlights.question: Is AI-led revenue incremental or cannibalised, and what is the pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: AI revenue of about INR15 crore is net new from new and existing clients; the pipeline is INR100-150 crore across stages. Management is building dedicated AI sales and solutioning teams.

qa_highlights.question: Is double-digit FY27 revenue growth guidance still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not reaffirm it. Its priority is margin improvement, and it asked investors to track profitability and ROE rather than revenue.

risks_watch: Book-to-bill of about 11-13% and TCV of INR205 crore below ambition; watch whether the deferred bookings land in Q2 and Q3 as management expects.
DSO at 82 days (up 7 days QoQ) with higher receivables and unbilled balances; Q2 focus is converting these to cash.
Wage cost step-up of about INR10 crore per quarter from labour codes and state minimum wage revisions; client repricing and cost-of-living talks are not yet concluded.
Margin path depends on repricing and exits of low-margin accounts; FY27 200 bps EBITDA expansion reiterated but no quarterly margin path given.
Alldigi-related governance: standalone profitability is weak excluding Alldigi, legal merger has no timeline, and central costs are only partly cross-charged.
Revenue growth guidance was not reaffirmed and the FY31 USD 1 billion target has no revised growth path; headcount expected to decline over the next couple of quarters.
key_quotes: We are not going to chase top line for its own sake.
We believe Q1 is the trough on margins, and we are working towards EBITDA margin expansion in FY27.
Revenue is not the only metric we are managing for this year.
We will not go and do one big acquisition.
As a management team, we do not see that as one of the options that we will execute, Aditya.
summary.management_tone: Confident on strategy and the margin-trough narrative, but cautious and non-committal on revenue: management declined to reaffirm double-digit FY27 growth and said it will give percentage growth paths in later quarters. Answers on Alldigi consolidation, the timeline for the USD 1 billion target and M&A funding were deliberately open-ended.

growth.why: Management reiterated ~200 bps FY27 EBITDA margin expansion and said Q1 is the margin trough, but de-emphasised the double-digit revenue growth target and gave no revenue guidance; TCV of INR205 cr fell below ambition and no capacity additions or capex were discussed, so growth backing is vague.
